solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poet's mama is strangely changing colour for some reason

indicators.note: something done strangely is done out of its normal way, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: eleven letters taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A poet's mother keeps oddly changing colour, and nobody knows why.
explanation.walkthrough: APOSEMATISM is the biological term for warning coloration, as in wasps or poison frogs; the definition is loose, since the colour serves a purpose rather than changing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aposematism is an animal's conspicuous warning coloration, colour adopted for the reason of deterring predators.

clue.text: Plant — horse eats one in Scotland

indicators.note: something that eats takes another thing inside it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a small horse
ae is the Scots word for one

explanation.surface: A horse grazing on a plant somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: PAEONY is an older spelling of peony.
explanation.definitionFit: The paeony, or peony, is a garden flower with large showy blooms, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Experienced person in Newgate?

parts.note: surface reading: someone held in the notorious London jail
setter's reading: Newgate is a former prison, and bird is slang for prison, so it is literally an aged jail

explanation.surface: A seasoned convict inside Newgate prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was London's old jail, demolished in 1904; 'bird' is British slang for prison (from rhyming slang birdlime, time), so Newgate is an old bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An old bird is an idiom for a wily, seasoned person who has seen it all before.

clue.text: Rested outside university compound in Glasgow?

indicators.note: one word sits outside another, wrapping around it

parts.note: sat down, took a rest
standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Someone took a break outside a university building in Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasgow stands for Scots usage; 'compound' is the chemical sense, not a walled enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Saut is the Scots form of salt, a chemical compound of sodium and chlorine.

clue.text: Seaweed from liquid realm

indicators.note: liquid things flow and lose their shape, so the next word's letters are poured into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Seaweed gathered from the watery kingdom of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Maerl is a hard red coralline alga that forms beds on the seabed, a kind of seaweed.

clue.text: Instrument given new steel covering

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the following word's letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written
a cope is a long cloak worn by clergy

explanation.surface: A tool gets a fresh steel casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A telescope is an optical instrument for viewing distant objects.

clue.text: Drizzle in southern commune overlooking river

indicators.note: in a down entry, to overlook is to sit above, so these pieces come first

parts.note: abbreviation for south or southern
a mir was a Russian peasant commune
abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Light rain falls on a commune in the south beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: MIR, the old Russian village commune, is a regular in harder puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Smirr is a Scots word for fine rain, the same thing as drizzle.

clue.text: No longer occupy island, unconditional leader having been deposed

indicators.note: a deposed leader is removed from the front, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the Isle of Man
pure in the sense of absolute, unqualified

explanation.surface: An ousted ruler must leave the island and give up holding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete sense: MANURE once meant to hold or occupy land, before it meant dung.
explanation.definitionFit: In its archaic sense manure meant to hold, occupy or cultivate land, so it is an obsolete verb for occupy.

clue.text: Trading ends sadly, making one very troubled

indicators.note: things that end sadly go wrong, so the letters before it end up disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper closes the business and is left deeply worried.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of angst, or existential anxiety, is greatly disturbed and uneasy.

clue.text: Friend accompanying an old man to get shelter from the sun

parts.note: a pal is a friend
the indefinite article
old man is slang for father, pa

explanation.surface: A friend and an elderly man go looking for shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A palapa is a Mexican open-sided thatched hut, built for shade on beaches.

clue.text: Each prominent feature penned by journalists showing tendency to moralise

indicators.note: to be penned is to be enclosed, so the first pieces go inside the journalists

parts.note: the press, journalists collectively
EA is the abbreviation for each
a jutting chin is a prominent facial feature

explanation.surface: Every reporter writes up something conspicuous with a sermonising slant.
explanation.definitionFit: Preachiness is the quality of lecturing others on morals, an inclination to sermonise.

clue.text: Old fellow with small body attached to knight

indicators.note: one piece joined onto the next, placed side by side

parts.note: a gemma is a small bud-like body by which some plants reproduce
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: An elderly man, slightly built, has a knight as his companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemman is an old colloquial contraction of gentleman, so an archaic word for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Embarrassed little wife revived

parts.note: red in the face
ux is the short form of Latin uxor, wife

explanation.surface: A shy young wife perks up again.
explanation.definitionFit: Redux, placed after a noun, means brought back or restored, as in a revived film or style.

clue.text: Story about academic engineer generating fuel in Scotland

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the story is read backwards

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
DIng is the abbreviation for Doctor of Engineering

explanation.surface: A tale about a university engineer who produces fuel in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academic engineer' is one unit: an engineer with a doctorate, DIng (Latin Doctor Ingeniariae).
explanation.definitionFit: Eilding, or eldin, is a Scots word for fuel such as peat or firewood.

clue.text: After hostilities extravagant speaker is one offering guarantees

indicators.note: one thing coming after another puts the speaker behind the hostilities

parts.note: war is a state of hostilities
someone who rants speaks wildly

explanation.surface: Once fighting ends, a bombastic orator promises everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranter is someone who gives a warranty, that is, a guarantee or assurance.

clue.text: Strip of material that is kept in room

indicators.note: something kept in a place is held within it

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for room
i.e., Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A piece of fabric stored in a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A riem is a South African rawhide thong, a narrow strip of leather.

clue.text: Earthenware pot mostly used in vineyards

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a cruse is a small earthenware jar

explanation.surface: Clay jars are commonly found in wine estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vineyards' looks like the place the pot is used, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cru is a French vineyard or its graded wine, so crus is the plural meaning vineyards.

clue.text: Saint wandering around African country — one like Francis of Assisi?

indicators.note: goes round the outside of the country, enclosing it
a wandering thing strays from its path, so the letters of the saint are moved about

parts.note: taken as written
Mali is a West African state

explanation.surface: A saint roaming across Africa, like Francis who preached to birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a definition by example: Francis of Assisi is the patron saint of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: An animalist is a champion of animal rights, and Francis of Assisi is famed for his love of creatures.

clue.text: Pay in advance for a function, sparing nothing

indicators.note: to spare something is to leave it out, and nothing is the zero letter that gets omitted

parts.note: taken as written
a role is a function or job

explanation.surface: Settle the bill early for an event, holding nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: Nothing is O, the round zero; removing it from a role leaves the answer. ARLE is Scots for giving earnest money, from arles, a deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: To arle is a Scots verb meaning to give earnest money, a deposit paid up front to secure a bargain.

clue.text: Strip machine almost to the bottom

indicators.note: going almost to the bottom of a down entry stops one short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a lathe is a turning machine

explanation.surface: Take a machine apart nearly down to its base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' looks like a verb, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lath is a thin narrow strip of wood, as used under plaster.

clue.text: Gosh, the first person to hide inside and show fear!

indicators.note: something hiding inside is tucked into the middle of another word

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh
we is the first person plural pronoun

explanation.surface: Goodness, the first man in hides away, afraid!
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first person' is grammar, a pronoun, not the earliest arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch or shrink back in fear.

clue.text: Ewe possibly as one of a minority flock (7, two words)

parts.note: surface reading: a sheep belonging to a small flock
setter's reading: the two-word answer read as an instruction, a short word's letters set loose, could give the word ewe

explanation.surface: A sheep that belongs to a small flock.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wee Frees are members of the Free Church of Scotland, a small Presbyterian body; a church congregation is its flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wee Free belongs to the minority Free Church of Scotland, and a congregation is traditionally called a flock.

clue.text: The female taking in journalist for religious instruction

indicators.note: taking something in means enclosing it, so the journalist goes inside

parts.note: her, the female pronoun
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A woman lets a reporter in for a scripture lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A heder is a traditional Jewish school where children receive religious teaching.

clue.text: Snake Greek character found in valley to the north

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it
in a down entry, heading north means going upwards, against the reading direction

parts.note: a dale is a valley
pi is a Greek letter

explanation.surface: A snake with Greek markings is discovered in a northern valley.
explanation.definitionFit: An elapid is a member of the cobra family of venomous snakes.

clue.text: A manuscript containing old piece of scripture

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the manuscript holds the next item within it

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An ancient manuscript holds a fragment of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: Curse man who deals in rupees?

parts.note: a ban is a curse or anathema
a man's name

explanation.surface: Damn the fellow who trades in Indian money.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers a definition by description: the rupee is India's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A banian is a Hindu merchant or trader, so someone who handles rupees.

clue.text: Rod applied to kiddie's bottom brings hatred

indicators.note: one thing applied to another is laid against it, so the pieces join

parts.note: a spit is a rod for roasting meat

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down entry is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of kiddie

explanation.surface: Caning a child's backside breeds resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite is malice, a desire to hurt someone, close to hatred.

clue.text: A pert lad's done body-building exercise

indicators.note: done in the sense of done in, wrecked, so the letters are broken up and remade

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A cheeky young man has finished his gym session.
explanation.definitionFit: A lat spread is a bodybuilding pose flexing the latissimus muscles of the back to show width.

clue.text: Item of archaeological interest curator finally housed in building

indicators.note: something housed in a building is placed inside it

parts.note: a shed is a simple building

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of curator

explanation.surface: A museum curator ends up storing a relic in an outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A sherd, or shard, is a broken fragment of pottery, a staple find on archaeological digs.

clue.text: Leather a vessel brought form the east

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means travelling right to left, against the reading direction

parts.note: taken as written
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: Leather goods shipped in from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints 'form', a slip for 'from'. Vessel suggests a ship, but here it is a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Napa is a soft leather made from sheepskin or lambskin, named after Napa in California.

clue.text: Mother has no yen for masquerade, keeping quiet

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: an affectionate word for mother
Y is the symbol for the yen

explanation.surface: Mum, wanting nothing, quietly takes part in a fancy-dress ball.
explanation.walkthrough: MUMM, or mum, is an old verb for acting in a mummers' play, a masked show traditionally performed in dumb show.
explanation.definitionFit: To mumm is to go mumming, playing in disguise as a silent masked performer.

clue.text: What may be in envelope — it peels apart

indicators.note: taken apart, the letters are pulled to pieces and put back differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An envelope's flap comes unstuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peels' hints at an envelope seal, but the words are only letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a letter, the kind of thing sealed inside an envelope.

clue.text: Scientist whoops endlessly about uranium

indicators.note: goes around the next item, surrounding it
without an end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: whoops as a plural noun, loud cries
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A scientist keeps exclaiming in alarm over uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whoops' looks like an exclamation of error, but it is the plural noun, shouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie and Pierre Curie were physicists famed for their research on radioactivity.

clue.text: Priest about to give report on action

indicators.note: about can mean moved round or every which way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleric is about to brief us on the operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitrep, short for situation report, is a military update on the state of an operation.

clue.text: Artist with design following a logical system

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician
to mean is to intend or design

explanation.surface: A painter plans according to a rational scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Petrus Ramus was a 16th-century French logician whose method of logic had many followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramean describes an adherent of Ramus's system of logic, a follower of that logical scheme.

clue.text: Insane once about woman at match getting medical treatment

indicators.note: goes around the woman, enclosing her

parts.note: dement is an obsolete adjective for mad
a match here is a marriage, and the bride is the woman in it

explanation.surface: A formerly mad woman at a football game is taken for hospital care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests sport, but it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Debridement is the surgical removal of dead or infected tissue from a wound.
